newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian YUKOS sees three pct crude oil output slip.
newsitem.headline: Russian YUKOS sees three pct crude oil output slip.

text.p: Russia's second largest oil producer, NK YUKOS, said on Thursday that crude oil output, including production by joint ventures, fell to 26.52 million tonnes (530,400 barrels per day, or bpd) over January-September.
It blamed the three percent drop on the fact that 38 percent of the company's nearly 15,300 wells were idle.
YUKOS' main producer, Yuganskneftegaz, produced 19.77 million tonnes over the period, also a decline of three percent on year-ago levels.
No absolute comparison figures were provided, but a company news release said that overall output exceeded planned levels.
NK YUKOS drilled fewer new wells over January-September -- 303 compared to 405 during the preceding year's period.

The group refined 11.27 million tonnes of crude over the first nine months of this year, and produced 143,300 tonnes of gasoline, 3.49 million tonnes of diesel and 4.13 million tonnes of heavy fuel oil (mazut).
YUKOS said that state oil pipeline monopoly Transneft had restricted YUKOS oil shipments, resulting in a loss of 398,000 tonnes of crude.

YUKOS, Russia's second largest oil company in terms of output and reserves, said in April that the firm and its joint ventures produced 34 million tonnes (683,940 bpd) in 1995, or 11.2 percent of Russia's total.
It had forecast output, not including production by joint ventures, to slip nearly eight percent this year to 31.1 million tonnes (626,000 barrels per day).
Nearly all of Russia's oil companies are struggling to reverse years of steep output declines.
